statement.p: Find the volume of the wedge-shaped region (Figure 1) contained in the cylinder x^2+y^2=49 and bounded above by the plane z=x and below by the xy-plane.

static.solution:
[Step 1.] Express \mathcal{W} in cylindrical coordinates. \mathcal{W} is bounded above by the plane z=x and below by z=0,
therefore 0\le z\le x, in particular x\ge 0. Hence, \mathcal{W} projects onto the semicircle \mathcal{D} in the xy-plane of radius 7, where x\ge 0.
r = 7
In polar coordinates, \mathcal{D} :\,-\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2},\ 0\le r\le 7 The upper surface is z=x=r \cos \theta and the lower surface is z=0. Therefore, \mathcal{W} :\,-\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2},\ 0\le r\le 7,\ 0\le z\le r \cos \theta
[Step 2.] Set up an integral in cylindrical coordinates and evaluate. The volume of \mathcal{W} is the triple integral \int\!\!\int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{W}} 1 \,dV.
Using change of variables in cylindrical coordinates gives \int\!\!\int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{W}} 1 \,dV = \int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \int_0^{7} \int_0^{r \cos \theta } r \,dz \,dr \,d\theta= \int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \int_0^{7} rz\bigg|_{z=0}^{r \cos \theta }dr \,d\theta=\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \int_0^{7} {r}^2 \cos \theta \,dr \,d\theta= \int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \frac{{r}^3}{3} \cos \theta \bigg|_{r=0}^{7} \,d\theta= \int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \frac{7^3}{3} \cos \theta \,d\theta =\frac{7^3}{3} \sin \theta \bigg|_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}= \frac{7^3}{3} \left( \sin \frac{\pi }{2}- \sin \left(-\frac{\pi }{2}\right)\right)= 228.667
